info.name: Preservica - monthly stats (for the DCDS sheet)
info.description:
# Monthly Preservica figures for the DCDS stats sheet

*Version 2026-11-03d.* Request 7 (debug) shows the version too. If it shows an older one, or no version, you're running an old copy: delete the older copies of this collection in Postman.

Measures Preservica and shows the month's figures laid out like the **DCDS_stats** Google Sheet, with a CSV to download, so you can copy them into the sheet by hand. Nothing in Preservica is changed.

**Before you start:** on this collection's **Variables** tab, fill in `username` and `password` in the **Current value** column (current values stay on your computer; initial values sync to Postman's servers), then click **Save**.

## Each month

1. Run it on the last day of the month or in the first five days of the next. In the first five days of a month it reports the month that just ended. To choose a month yourself, set `month` (e.g. `2026-10`).
2. Click the collection's **⋯** menu > **Run collection**, keep every request ticked, and click **Run**. It makes several requests per asset, so a few hundred assets take a few minutes; the **Console** shows progress. You can also **Send** requests 1 to 6 one at a time: request 5 then measures one asset per send, so for hundreds of assets use Run collection. Wait for each send to finish, and send it again until its **Visualize** tab says all assets are done (Postman keeps a request's results only when it finishes).
3. Open **6. Show the monthly figures** and its **Visualize** tab. It shows:
   - **DCDS tab: Preservica rows** (#Collections, #Assets, #Images, #SoundRecordings, #MovingImages, #Text, #Downloads), with a box of the seven values: copy it, click the month's cell in the #Collections row, and paste;
   - **Storage tab: Tier 1** #TBPreservicaHot and #TBPreservicaCold, in TB;
   - **Preservica tab:** about 45 detailed rows (category, metric, value): one box to paste at A3 the first time (labels and values in the month's column), and a values-only box for later months;
   - a **Download CSV** button for everything (columns Tab, Category, Metric and the month).

## What the figures mean

- **DCDS rows are what was added that month** (records created in the month), like the tab's other monthly rows. Set `dcdsCounts` to `total` for all-time totals instead.
- **#Downloads** is the change in Preservica's all-time download counter since last month. Postman remembers each month's all-time figure (`downloadsHistory`), so the first month is blank. To fill it anyway, put last month's all-time count in `previousDownloadsAllTime` and send request 6 again (clear it afterwards).
- **TB are decimal** (10^12 bytes): 2 decimal places for the Storage tab, 4 on the Preservica tab. A file kept in two storage locations counts in both for Stored, Hot and Cold, and once for Content.
- **Hot or Cold** comes from the storage location's name: names matching `coldPattern` (default `glacier|deep|cold|archive|tape|offline`) are Cold, so `S3 Deep Glacier Adapter` is Cold.
- **Images, sound, moving images and text** come from each asset's Preservation format group (`pdf` counts as Text, `tiff` as Images and so on). The FormatGroups rows list every group found, so you can check the sorting.
- **Integrity** rows come from each file's integrity check history. Set `integrityChecks` to `false` to skip them (one request fewer per file).
- **Duplicates** are files whose SHA1 checksum also appears in another asset.

## If something goes wrong

- The yellow boxes on the report say what's missing and why. HTTP 401 or 403 means the account needs the **Access** functional role with **Read Metadata** and **Read Content**.
- The report's **What the run found** table shows where data went missing, such as assets found but not measured, or assets without a created date or format group.
- Send **7. Debug: show raw responses** on its own after a run. Its **Visualize** tab shows what the last run collected, and Preservica's raw answers to each kind of request: the top-level folders, both searches (with the fields returned), and one asset followed down to a file. Put a reference in `debugAsset` to follow a particular asset. It shows no password or token, so the page can be sent to whoever maintains the collection.

console.log(`Logged in. Reporting ${name} ${y}. Later requests log in again by themselves when the token nears its 15-minute limit.`);

exec: // Shows Preservica's raw answers for each kind of request this collection makes,
// and what the last run collected, so missing data can be traced. Nothing is changed.
const send = (url, body) => new Promise((ok, fail) => {
if (body) { r.method = 'POST'; r.body = { mode: 'urlencoded', urlencoded: body }; }
steps.push({ name, url: short(url), code: res ? res.code : 'error', body: body.slice(0, 4000), note: note || '' });
const first = (text, re) => { const m = text.match(re); return m ? m[1].trim() : ''; };
const search = (type, fields) => [{ key: 'start', value: '0' }, { key: 'max', value: '3' },
{ key: 'q', value: JSON.stringify({ q: '*', fields: [{ name: 'xip.document_type', values: [type] }].concat(fields.map(f => ({ name: f, values: [] }))) }) }]
// 1. Top-level folders (the answer to this request itself).
show('1 top-level folders', pm.request.url.toString(), pm.response, 'Each <Child type="SO"> is a collection.');
// 2 and 3. The two searches, first 3 results each, asking for the same fields as the run.
show('2 folder search', searchUrl, await send(searchUrl, search('SO', ['xip.created'])),
'totalHits is the folder count; each result should have xip.created.');
const assetsJson = show('3 asset search', searchUrl, await send(searchUrl, search('IO', ['xip.created', 'xip.top_level_so',
'totalHits is the asset count. Each result lists the fields Preservica returned; a field missing here is blank for that asset.');
// 4 to 10. One asset followed down to a file.
const repsXml = show('4 representations', repsUrl, await send(repsUrl), `Asset ${ref}. Each <Representation type="..."> links to one representation.`);
const repXml = repUrl ? show('5 representation', repUrl, await send(repUrl), 'Lists the content objects in it.') : '';
const gensXml = gensUrl ? show('6 generations', gensUrl, await send(gensUrl), 'Every version of the file; active="true" is the current one.') : '';
const genXml = genUrl ? show('7 generation', genUrl, await send(genUrl), 'The original/active flags, FormatGroup, and the links to its files.') : '';
show('8 file', bsUrl, await send(bsUrl), 'FileSize and the SHA1 checksum.');

await send(`${bsUrl}/integrity-check-history?start=0&max=10`), 'Each check has a Date and Success.');
const where = !repsXml ? 'step 4' : !repUrl ? 'step 4 (no representation link)' : !co ? 'step 5 (no content object)'
console.log(`Couldn't follow the asset to a file: it stopped at ${where}. The answer shown for that step has the real layout.`);
steps.push({ name: `Stopped at ${where}`, url: '', code: '', body: '', note: "The collection couldn't find the next link in the answer above." });
} else console.log('No asset to follow: the asset search found nothing.');

tag: a[3] || '(none)', group: a[4] || '(none)', downloads: a[5] === null ? '(none)' : a[5] }));
